# Sirach 14 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 14 (27 verses)
**Total Disagreements:** 15

---

## Disagreement 1 — Verse 1

**Issue:** "Has not stumbled through his speech" — the nature of the stumbling
- EMET: "who has not stumbled through his speech, and who has not been stabbed by the pain of sin"
- LOGOS: "who has not slipped because of his speech, and who has not been pierced by the pangs of sin"
- PNEUMA: "who hasn't let careless words get them into trouble, and who doesn't carry the sting of guilt"
- SOPHIA: "who has not stumbled through his speech, and who has not been stabbed by the pain of sin"

**Resolution:** EMET/SOPHIA "stumbled" is close to the Greek ὀλίσθησεν. LOGOS "slipped" is also valid. PNEUMA paraphrases. "Stabbed by the pain" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "pierced by the pangs" (LOGOS) — both valid. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 2 — Verse 3

**Issue:** "Miser" — Greek mikropsychos (small-souled)
- EMET: "a miser"
- LOGOS: "a small-minded man"
- PNEUMA: "someone who hoards it grudgingly"
- SOPHIA: "a small-minded man"

**Resolution:** Greek μικρόψυχος literally means "small-souled" — "small-minded" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) captures this better than "miser" which is more about money. SOPHIA adopted LOGOS rendering.

---

## Disagreement 3 — Verse 4

**Issue:** "Gathers" vs. "accumulates" — and who benefits
- EMET: "gathers for others; and others will feast on his goods"
- LOGOS: "accumulates for others; and strangers will enjoy his goods"
- PNEUMA: "saving for someone else — strangers will end up enjoying"
- SOPHIA: "accumulates for others; and strangers will enjoy his goods"

**Resolution:** LOGOS "accumulates" slightly more formal than "gathers." "Strangers" (LOGOS/PNEUMA/SOPHIA) more specific than "others" (EMET). SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 4 — Verse 6

**Issue:** "Punishment of his wickedness" vs. "retribution for his evil"
- EMET: "the punishment of his wickedness"
- LOGOS: "the retribution for his evil"
- PNEUMA: "their just punishment"
- SOPHIA: "the punishment of his wickedness"

**Resolution:** EMET/SOPHIA "wickedness" retains moral weight. LOGOS "retribution" more legalistic. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 5 — Verse 7

**Issue:** "Through forgetfulness" vs. "by accident"
- EMET: "he does it through forgetfulness"
- LOGOS: "he does it by accident"
- PNEUMA: "it happens almost by accident"
- SOPHIA: "he does it almost by accident"

**Resolution:** Greek ἀκουσίως means "involuntarily/unintentionally" — not literally forgetting. LOGOS "by accident" is more idiomatic. SOPHIA adopted LOGOS with PNEUMA's "almost" qualifier. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 6 — Verse 8

**Issue:** "Turns away his face" — the gesture of the miser
- EMET: "he turns away his face and disregards people"
- LOGOS: "he averts his face and disregards others"
- PNEUMA: "they look away and have no concern for anyone else"
- SOPHIA: "he turns away his face and disregards others"

**Resolution:** Minor variation. EMET/SOPHIA preserve the gesture. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 7 — Verse 12

**Issue:** "The covenant of Hades" — how to render this unusual phrase
- EMET: "the covenant of Hades has not been shown to you"
- LOGOS: "the covenant of Hades has not been shown to you"
- PNEUMA: "you don't know how long you have; no one has been shown the terms of Hades' contract"
- SOPHIA: "the terms of Hades have not been shown to you"

**Resolution:** Greek διαθήκη = covenant/decree/terms. All agents agree on the meaning — no one knows their death date. PNEUMA paraphrases expansively. SOPHIA slightly paraphrases "covenant" as "terms." The phrase "covenant of Hades" is striking and worth preserving more closely. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 8 — Verse 16

**Issue:** "Beguile your soul" vs. "indulge yourself" vs. "indulge your soul"
- EMET: "beguile your soul"
- LOGOS: "indulge yourself"
- PNEUMA: "enjoy the pleasures of life"
- SOPHIA: "indulge your soul"

**Resolution:** Greek εὔφρανε = to gladden, cheer up. "Indulge your soul" (SOPHIA) retains both the action and the object. "Beguile" (EMET) is archaic. PNEUMA's expansion loses the directness. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 9 — Verse 17

**Issue:** "Wears out like a garment" — the garment metaphor
- EMET: "All flesh grows old like a garment"
- LOGOS: "All flesh wears out like a garment"
- PNEUMA: "grows old and wears out like a garment" (combines both)
- SOPHIA: "All flesh wears out like a garment"

**Resolution:** Greek παλαιοῦται = to grow old, become worn out. LOGOS/SOPHIA "wears out" more precise. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 10 — Verse 18

**Issue:** Tree leaf metaphor — Ben Sira echoing Homer and Qohelet
- EMET: "some it sheds and some it grows"
- LOGOS: "some fall and some sprout"
- PNEUMA: "some fall while others push through"
- SOPHIA: "some it sheds and others it puts forth"

**Resolution:** The image echoes Iliad 6:146 and Qohelet. EMET/SOPHIA preserve the active subject (tree does the shedding). LOGOS/PNEUMA make leaves active. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 11 — Verse 19

**Issue:** "Works of corruption" vs. "work of corruption"
- EMET: "All the works of corruption will fail"
- LOGOS: "Every work of corruption will perish"
- PNEUMA: "Everything that is made will eventually fall apart"
- SOPHIA: "Every work of corruption will perish"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA loses "corruption" qualifier. LOGOS/SOPHIA use "perish" instead of "fail" — stronger. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 12 — Verse 22

**Issue:** "Goes after her like a tracker" vs. "hunter"
- EMET: "like a tracker"
- LOGOS: "like a hunter"
- PNEUMA: "like a tracker following a trail"
- SOPHIA: "like a hunter"

**Resolution:** Greek κυνηγός = hunter. LOGOS "hunter" is more literal. EMET/PNEUMA "tracker" adds an interpretive nuance. SOPHIA followed LOGOS. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 13 — Verse 24

**Issue:** "Camp beside her house" — the famous verse
- EMET: "He camps beside her house, and fastens his tent peg in her walls"
- LOGOS: "Who camps beside her house, and drives a tent peg into her walls"
- PNEUMA: "Who makes camp right outside her house, and drives a stake into her very walls"
- SOPHIA: "Who camps beside her house, and drives a tent peg into her walls"

**Resolution:** All agents essentially agree on this memorable verse. EMET/SOPHIA "tent peg" is more specific than PNEUMA "stake." SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 14 — Verse 25

**Issue:** "Settles in a good lodging place" vs. "lodges in a fine dwelling"
- EMET: "settles in a good lodging place"
- LOGOS: "lodges in a fine dwelling"
- PNEUMA: "makes their home in the best of places"
- SOPHIA: "lodges in a fine dwelling"

**Resolution:** Greek κατασκηνοῖ = pitches tent/lodges. LOGOS/SOPHIA close to literal. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 15 — Verse 27

**Issue:** "Lives in her glory" — what "glory" means here
- EMET: "he dwells in her glory"
- LOGOS: "dwells in her glory"
- PNEUMA: "lives in the light of her glory"
- SOPHIA: "dwells in her glory"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA's "light of" adds an interpretive gloss. EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA stay literal. SOPHIA adopted.
